speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your gums or other mucous membranes, and tiny red spots on your skin called petechiae. Can you tell me if you've ever had a similar episode before, and does it run in your family?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any bleeding after minor injuries that took longer to stop than usual, or is there a family history of similar bleeding problems? Also, when were you last vaccinated or given antibiotics? REQUEST TEST: PT/PTT/INR, Platelet_Count, Coagulation_Protein_Profile.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal), Platelet Count 280,000 /μL (normal), Coagulation Protein Profile: Normal. Note: ELISA Binding Assay shows Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous assessment seems incorrect; pneumonia does not cause petechiae or mucous membrane bleeding. Please clarify if the bleeding occurs spontaneously or only after trauma, and have you noticed any gum bleeding when brushing your teeth? REQUEST TEST: Bleeding_Time, Clotting_Time.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bleeding Time: Prolonged, Clotting Time: Normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The prolonged bleeding time with normal clotting time and the history of mucosal bleeding and petechiae strongly suggest a platelet disorder, most likely ITP in a young child. Please request a complete blood count with peripheral smear to confirm low platelet count and rule out other causes.
